format.discovery_delivery: separately edited vertical Shorts that point to full episodes

logline: In a fictional coastal West African city, a radio repairer restores a decommissioned emergency transmitter and begins receiving distress calls exactly one day before the events they describe. With an investigative journalist and a power-grid engineer, she follows the warnings into a buried civic secret—and discovers that changing tomorrow may make someone else's future worse.
series_premise: A grounded, character-led mystery about warning systems, public trust, memory, responsibility and the human cost of decisions made in secret. The science-fiction premise drives the plot, but the emotional story is about three people forced to decide what they owe one another and the city they call home.

setting.city_status: fictional coastal West African city; do not identify it as a real city
setting.visual_identity: recognisably coastal and West African without reducing the setting to tourist imagery or stereotypes

locations.name: Dike Radio Works
locations.description: A narrow, practical radio repair shop with a metal shutter, crowded shelves, soldering tools, old receivers and a workbench facing the street.

locations.name: Relay Station 6
locations.description: A decommissioned public-warning station on a raised service road near the coast; weathered concrete, rusted antenna structures and a locked equipment room.

locations.name: The Ledger newsroom
locations.description: A compact independent newsroom with old filing cabinets, recording equipment, paper archives and a view of the city.

locations.name: Aderin Grid Control
locations.description: A municipal power operations room with physical switchgear, restrained monitoring screens and an industrial service corridor.

locations.name: The Old Causeway
locations.description: A disused coastal road and flood-control crossing connected to the Night of Silence.

world_rules: A functioning receiver can capture the unexplained transmission only at 02:17 local time.
The message describes a verifiable event scheduled to occur approximately 24 hours later; it is incomplete and may contain noise, gaps or location clues.
A warning does not explain its own cause. Characters must investigate before acting.
Changing an event does not create an easy reset. Interventions have practical consequences and may change what is transmitted next.
The signal cannot answer arbitrary questions, identify every future event or solve the characters' problems for them.
The source of the signal remains unresolved through the first season; revelations must be earned through evidence and character choices.

backstory.description: Eighteen years before the pilot, Aderin Bay suffered a nineteen-minute citywide communications and power failure during a coastal storm. A public-warning trial was blamed for part of the confusion. The official inquiry closed quickly, and Relay Station 6 was decommissioned.
backstory.public_record: The LANTERN early-warning network was described as a failed municipal pilot and its records were archived.
backstory.dramatic_truth: The public record is incomplete. Several people who worked on LANTERN disappeared from the project files, and the system's final test was never properly explained.

themes: The responsibility that comes with knowing what may happen
Public trust and the consequences of institutional secrecy
Memory, grief and the stories cities choose to forget
The difference between preventing harm and controlling other people
Friendship built through difficult, imperfect choices

style_bible.animation: premium cinematic 3D animation with grounded human proportions and restrained stylisation
style_bible.lighting: motivated practical lighting, humid coastal night atmosphere, controlled highlights and natural skin tones
style_bible.camera: deliberate, readable cinematic framing; motivated movement; no random camera motion
style_bible.environments: physically coherent, recurring locations with stable geography, props, layout and weather continuity
style_bible.character_rendering: stable facial proportions, skin tone, hairstyle, age, body proportions and wardrobe across all shots
style_bible.sound: restrained environmental sound, distinct character voices, purposeful silence, original or properly licensed score

cast.name: Amara Dike
cast.backstory: Amara inherited Dike Radio Works after her father disappeared from public life following the Night of Silence. She has avoided the abandoned relay network because the official story never matched what her father told her.
cast.season_one_arc: Moves from treating the signal as a technical anomaly to accepting responsibility for what she does with the warnings; learns that her father's disappearance is tied to LANTERN.
cast.appearance_lock: A 27-year-old West African woman with deep brown skin, an oval face, alert dark-brown eyes, a small vertical scar through the outer edge of her left eyebrow, short natural coiled hair tapered at the sides, a lean practical build, a muted rust work jacket over a charcoal crew-neck shirt, dark utility trousers and worn black work boots. No changes to facial structure, scar, hair, skin tone or clothing palette between scenes unless the script explicitly records a costume change.

cast.season_one_arc: Moves from chasing a story to protecting the people caught inside it; discovers that a source he trusted helped bury part of the LANTERN record.

cast.season_one_arc: Moves from professional self-protection to taking responsibility for the systems he helped maintain; reveals his connection to the LANTERN archive.

voice_cast.notes: The initial Piper assignments are audition candidates, not final casting. The series must not ship with duplicated fallback voices or unapproved voice models. A replacement model must have an acceptable commercial-use licence and a successful audition.

episode_rules: Every episode must resolve its immediate dramatic problem while advancing at least one season-long mystery.
Every major character must make consequential choices; no character exists only to explain the plot.
No scene may exist solely to pad runtime. Each scene must change information, danger, relationship or direction.
Do not use humour, jokes, memes or gag reactions as a default engagement device.
Do not repeat a previous episode's central problem with only names and locations changed.
Do not contradict the world rules, character histories, established physical details or already-revealed evidence.
Do not invent a new recurring character or permanent location without updating the series bible.
End episodes with a meaningful consequence or unresolved question, not an arbitrary cut before the promised payoff.
